The question everyone asks

Will this hit your credit file?

Not until you choose an offer.

Asking for your options puts nothing on your credit file. A lender runs a check only with your consent, after you've seen the offers and decided to proceed with one.

Eligibility

Is your business eligible?

Your business qualifies if it

  • Has an active ABN
  • Has been trading for 6 months or more
  • Turns over $5,000 or more a month
  • Is a sole trader, partnership or company

Probably not the right loan if

  • The business hasn't started trading yet (ask about start-up options)
  • It needs more than $500,000 unsecured (a loan against property may suit better)
Straight answers

Before your business applies

An active ABN, at least 6 months of trading, and a minimum monthly turnover of $5,000 over the past 6 months. Sole traders and companies are both welcome.

For loans up to $250,000, 6 months of business bank statements and valid ID, uploaded through a secure link. Over $250,000, lenders usually also ask for financial statements, BAS and ATO transaction statements. PDF bank statements aren't accepted by lenders because of fraud risk, so the secure link does the work.

Pre-approval can come back in under an hour and approval in as little as 12 hours. Most approvals land within 24 to 48 hours of the full documents arriving, and funds are usually in the business account within 24 business hours of accepting the offer.

Rates start from 7.75% p.a.* for the strongest profiles. Across the panel, unsecured rates generally sit between 10% and 20% p.a. depending on industry, cash flow, credit history and the term. You see the actual rate in writing before you commit.

No collateral is taken over property or assets. Most lenders do ask the business owner for a personal guarantee, which means you'd be personally responsible if the business couldn't repay. Your broker explains what that means for you before you sign anything.

No. Lenders only run a credit check with your consent, after you've submitted a full application and chosen an offer. The initial options call doesn't touch your file.

There's no application fee. If a loan proceeds, an origination fee may apply, typically 2 to 4% of the loan amount, and you see the exact figure in your offer before you accept. The fee is only charged at settlement.

Often, yes. Several lenders on the panel look at current cash flow rather than past credit events. It's harder, and the rate is higher, but it's exactly the kind of file a broker with 110+ lenders can place that a single lender can't.

Most of them: hospitality, construction and trades, retail and ecommerce, transport, manufacturing, medical, professional services. If you're unsure, ask on the call.
